note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Costa Rica: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: From 1 January 2026 an employee's monthly pay is free of tax up to CRC 918,000, then taxed at 10% to 1,347,000, 15% to 2,364,000, 20% to 4,727,000 and 25% above, less monthly credits of CRC 1,710 per child and 2,590 for a spouse; there is no provincial or municipal income tax.
figures.applies: Salaried income from 1 January 2026 (Ley 7092 art. 33 as updated by Decreto 45333-H); tax is on Costa Rican-source income only

sources.said: a) Las rentas de hasta ¢918.000,00 (novecientos dieciocho mil colones) mensuales no estarán sujetas al impuesto. b) Sobre el exceso de ¢918.000,00 (novecientos dieciocho mil colones) mensuales y hasta ¢1.347.000,00 (un millón trescientos cuarenta y siete mil colones) mensuales, se pagará el diez por ciento (10%).

c) Sobre el exceso de ¢1.347.000,00 (un millón trescientos cuarenta y siete mil colones) mensuales y hasta ¢2.364.000,00 (dos millones trescientos sesenta y cuatro mil colones) mensuales, se pagará el quince por ciento (15%). d) Sobre el exceso de ¢2.364.000,00 (dos millones trescientos sesenta y cuatro mil colones) mensuales y hasta ¢4.727.000,00 (cuatro millones setecientos veintisiete mil colones) mensuales, se pagará el veinte por ciento (20%). e) Sobre el exceso de ¢4.727.000,00 (cuatro millones setecientos veintisiete mil colones) mensuales, se pagará el veinticinco por ciento (25%).
i. Por cada hijo, la suma de mil setecientos diez colones (¢1.710,00) ii. Por el cónyuge, la suma de dos mil quinientos noventa colones (¢2.590,00)
None of the provinces or municipalities impose any income taxes on individuals within their jurisdiction.

figures.finding: A self-employed person (a freelance actor, writer or director) pays on annual net income: nothing to CRC 6,244,000, 10% to 8,329,000, 15% to 10,414,000, 20% to 20,872,000 and 25% above, less annual credits of CRC 20,520 per child and 31,080 for a spouse.
figures.applies: Personas físicas con actividades lucrativas, fiscal year 2026 (Ley 7092 art. 15 c, as set by Ley 10667 and Decreto 45333-H)

sources.said: i) Las rentas de hasta ¢6.244.000,00 (seis millones doscientos cuarenta y cuatro mil colones) anuales, no estarán sujetas al impuesto. ii) Sobre el exceso de ¢6.244.000,00 (seis millones doscientos cuarenta y cuatro mil colones) anuales y hasta ¢8.329. 000,00 (ocho millones trescientos veintinueve mil colones) anuales, se pagará el diez por ciento (10%).

iv)Sobre el exceso de ¢10.414.000,00 (diez millones cuatrocientos catorce mil colones) anuales y hasta ¢20.872.000,00 (veinte millones ochocientos setenta y dos mil colones) anuales, se pagará el veinte por ciento (20%). v) Sobre el exceso de ¢20.872.000,00 (veinte millones ochocientos setenta y dos mil colones) anuales, se pagará el veinticinco por ciento (25%).
a) Por cada hijo el crédito fiscal será de veinte mil quinientos veinte colones (¢20.520,00) anuales

figures.finding: The fiscal year is the calendar year; employees file nothing (tax is withheld monthly); the self-employed file a return and pay the balance two and a half months after the year ends (by 15 March), with instalments during the year.

sources.said: Income Tax Law, Law number 7092, established the fiscal period will match the calendar year

Self-employed individuals are required to make instalments of estimated taxes, which are computed on the average of the last three fiscal years, and a final payment two and a half months after the end of the fiscal year.

figures.finding: From 2026 to 2028 an employee pays 10.83% of gross pay to the CCSS and allied funds (5.50% health and maternity, 4.33% pensions, 1% Banco Popular) and the employer 26.83% (14.83% to the CCSS plus 12% to other institutions and worker-protection funds), with no ceiling stated.
figures.applies: Employees, 2026-2028; the self-employed contribute at income-scaled rates not read

sources.said: Muerte (IVM) Subtotal CCSS 14.67% 9.67% 14.83% 9.83%
Del 1° de enero del 2026 al 31 de diciembre del 2028. 11,66% Patronos: 5,58% Trabajadores: 4,33%

figures.finding: The employer withholds the salary tax monthly from payroll; employees file no annual return for that income.

sources.said: Employees who receive salaries and other similar or complementary remunerations or benefits must pay a monthly income tax that is withheld by the employer from the monthly payroll. Individuals do not need to file an annual tax return for this type of income.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays only withholding: 25% of a payment for personal services rendered in Costa Rica (a performance, writing or directing), 25% on royalties, 30% on other income; the withholding settles the tax.

sources.said: Non-residents are liable only for the applicable withholding taxes (WHTs), depending on the nature of the local income.

Technical service and management fees, royalties, patents, trademarks, franchises, and formulas 25 Transportation and communication services 8.5 Personal services from a Costa Rican source 25 Others 30

individuals who stay in Costa Rica, continuously or discontinuously, for more than 183 days, including departures and arrivals to the country, during the same fiscal period are considered tax resident in Costa Rica.

figures.finding: VAT is 13% on goods and services, including services consumed in Costa Rica; the freelancer's registration threshold was not found.

sources.said: The standard applicable VAT rate is 13%;

figures.finding: A payment to a non-domiciled beneficiary for the use of films, television films, recordings and like means of spreading images or sounds bears a single and definitive 20% of the gross amount under article 59 (e) of Ley 7092, radio and television serials (telenovelas) 50% under (f); no special rule for a resident author's royalties was found.
figures.applies: remittances abroad for the use of a film, a television film or a recording; a resident's royalties are ordinary income (no special rule found)
